questions.prompt: A motor sheet lists a stall torque of 548 mNm and a rated torque of 72.2 mNm. You must hold a load for several minutes. Which row do you compare the load torque with?
options: The stall torque, because it is the largest torque the motor can produce.
The rated torque (continuous limit), because holding a load for minutes is continuous duty.
The no-load torque, because it is the first row of the sheet.
Neither: the stall torque divided by two.
questions.explanation: Stall torque is reached only at zero speed and the stall current heats the winding within seconds; the rated torque is the thermal limit for continuous duty.

questions.prompt: A motor sheet lists a nominal voltage of 24 V and a terminal resistance of 1.63 ohm. Stall current in amperes (U/R).
questions.explanation: At stall there is no back-EMF, so I = U/R = 24/1.63 = 14.72 A.

questions.prompt: A stepper sheet gives a holding torque of 3.17 kgf-cm. Convert it to N m (1 kgf = 9.80665 N).
A motor has a speed constant of 250 rpm/V. Its torque constant in mNm/A (kt = 60/(2 pi kv)). Precision 0.3.
questions.explanation: kt = 60/(2 pi 250) = 0.03820 N m/A = 38.2 mNm/A; the sheet prints 38.3.

questions.prompt: Why does the pull-out torque of a stepper at a high step rate depend on the driver supply voltage?
options: A higher voltage makes the magnets stronger.
A higher voltage lowers the winding resistance.
A higher voltage lets the winding current rise faster through its L/R time constant, so more current flows in each short step.
It does not: the curve depends only on the motor.
questions.explanation: Winding current rises exponentially with time constant L/R; at a high step rate the step is short, so a higher voltage is needed to reach the current (TI AN-828).

questions.prompt: A motor produces 0.0722 N m at its rated point. With a 14:1 planetary gearhead of 85 % efficiency, what is the output torque in N m? Precision 0.005.
A motor's rated current is 2.36 A at 22 C ambient with a 155 C winding limit. Estimate the continuous current at 60 C ambient in amperes (scale by sqrt((Tmax - Ta)/(Tmax - 22))). Precision 0.03.
A hobby listing says 'stall torque 25 kg-cm' and nothing else about voltage, resistance or rated torque. Describe how you would audit it before using it in a robot.
rubric: Notes that the voltage is missing and a torque in kg-cm without a voltage cannot be used; asks for or measures the voltage conditions.
Asks for the terminal resistance (to derive stall current U/R and kt) and the rated or continuous torque and current, since stall is not a working value.
Proposes consistency checks or bench measurements (no-load speed and current, resistance) and a derating margin before committing.
questions.explanation: Rubric-guided: compare your answer with each rubric point; this question is not automatically graded.
